exposure: Early Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR) based on Doppler-inclusive criteria
Late Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR) based on Doppler-inclusive criteria
Small for Gestational Age (SGA) based on Doppler-inclusive criteria
cohort: The study included 160 fetuses initially diagnosed with Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR) based on the Japanese criterion (estimated fetal weight below -1.5 standard deviations), after excluding cases with fetal malformation, who were then reclassified into early FGR, late FGR, or SGA.
finding: The early FGR group, as classified by Doppler-inclusive criteria, showed significantly higher incidences of preterm birth, emergent Cesarean section, and severe maternal or neonatal complications compared to late FGR and SGA groups.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery, specifically emergent Cesarean section, was significantly higher in the early Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR) group as classified by Doppler-inclusive criteria.
birth_weight: Fetuses included had an estimated fetal weight (EFW) below -1.5 standard deviations based on the Japanese criterion.
gest_age: N/A (gestational age at delivery was an outcome, and gestational age at diagnosis was a factor in reclassification, but a specific range for the entire cohort is not provided).
